text: Assault Rave (Japanese: , Asarutoreivu) is Addam's Level II Special in . As with Addam's other specials, the element of Assault Rave is determined by the Greatsword he has equipped.
Army Arachnos are enemies in . They are members of the Arachno family, and can be found at level 23 in the Urayan Tunnels.
Art of Subjugation (Japanese: , Senjutsu: Senshō Tōbatsu) is Taion's Chain Art in .

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Armored Linings are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Gamma Commissary. The legendary variant can be purchased from the Prize X-change Blue, or dropped by Rambler Curalie. In , the common variant can be purchased from the Elevator Landing Caravan.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Assist Belts are Accessories in . The common variant can be purchased from the Drahaga Store.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Aural Enhance Sensors are Accessories in and . The Ultra Aural Sensor and Sonic Sensor have a stronger version of this accessory's effect.

The Atoll Ferronis Hulk (Japanese: , Kanshō no Kuchita Tetsukyoshin) is a Rest Spot in . It is located on the Baldotas Atoll in Erythia Sea. To activate this Ferronis Hulk, the party must complete the quest The Atoll Hulk, and requires 25 Ether Cylinders to reboot. The Atoll Caravan is located here.
The Ascension Grounds (Japanese: , Tenkan no Shokeijō) are a Landmark in . It is located in Agnus Castle of the Agnus Castle Region. It is where Mio goes through her Homecoming Ceremony.
The Arsenal Control Room (Japanese: , Kōshō Seigyoshitsu) is a Rest Spot in . It is located at Ferronis Arsenal #2 in the Origin Interior.
The Arms Storage Tower, Lower (Japanese: , Kasō Heisō Hokantō) is a Landmark in , located in the Origin Interior.
Armored Chestnuts are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be purchased from the Colony 30 Caravan, or the Tableland Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

Arrow Ignas are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 18 on Ribbi Flats, level 43 on Elaice Highway, and at level 98 in Rebellion Cave at Erythia Sea.

Assembly Conductors are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Keves Castle Region. They can also be produced from the Perimeter Outlet Fabricator after the first step of Colony 0 renovation.
Atmos Sapphires are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Keves Castle Region. They can also be produced from the Perimeter Outlet Fabricator after the first step of Colony 0 renovation.

|-|XC3 = |-|FR = Armu Barleys are Plant Collectibles in and . They can be found in the Cadensia Region in . They can also be produced from the Atoll Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They can be found on the Aurora Shelf in .
Aspid Fossils are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be produced from the Sandbar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They are fossilized Aspids.
Aries Furs are items in and . It is commonly dropped by Mant Aries, Little Aries, and Costa Aries, along with being dropped by the Unique Monster Stonehoof Torphan.
Arpat Anloods (Japanese: , Arubāto Haindo) are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Anlood family, and can be found at level 87 - 88 in The Cavity of Swordmarch.
Armored Rhinons are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Rhinon family, and can be found at level 46-48 at the Great Sword's Base and in Erythia Sea in the Cadensia Region.
Assassin Antols are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Antol family, and can be found at level 58-59 in the Antol Pit in Erythia Sea.

Armuvore Aligos (Japanese: , Arumakui Diburo) are Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Aligo family, and can be found at level 48 at Colony Mu in the Erythia Sea during To Face Forward.
Arms Storage Tower, Upper, or the Upper Storage Tower (Japanese: , Jōsō Heisō Hokantō), is a Rest Spot in . It is located at the Central Defense in the Origin Interior.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Asylum Linings are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the O'Virbus Commissary and Handypon. The legendary variant can be obtained from Talkative Dirakha. In , the common variant can be purchased from the Colony 9 Supply Office.
The Atoll Caravan is a shop in . It is run by a Traderpon and is located at the Atoll Ferronis Hulk in Erythia Sea.

Ascension Caravan is a shop in . It is run by the Ascended Traderpon and can be found at the Ascension Grounds in the Agnus Castle Region upon reaching Affinity Level 2 with Agnus Castle. It sells Cadensia Region Collectibles.

Armu Psychology is a Key Item in . It is the first volume of a two-book set, with the second volume being Ardun Psychology, and details how one should raise of Armus. Both volumes can be purchased for 5000 G from Wellwell's Emporium during The Future I Want to Spin.
Army Satchels are Sell-Only Collectible items in . They can be found in Origin.
Armeh Taos are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Taos family, and can be found at level 16-17 in the Eagus Wilderness.
Arogan Ansels are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Ansel family, and can be found at level 21-22 near Sparres Barr and at level 55 on Isla Passerat in Ribbi Flats.

The Assassin Moramora is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Moramora family, and is fought at level 59 at the Colony Mu, Respite Ranch in Erythia Sea after Nandun is born during the informal Ardun ranch quest.
Atomize (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is one of Taion's Ouroboros arts.

Arts and Crafts is a Time Attack Challenge Battle in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from the second part of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least an A rank for the first time will unlock the Swimwear B outfit for Sena.

Attack Down is a Status Effect in and . It decreases enemy or player attack when it is cast. A separate debuff known as Flame Clock Low, Attack Down exists during the first chapter when the party is still under the control of the Flame Clock with an identical attack decrease.

Armor Veil is a Status Effect in and . It nullifies a certain amount of damage dealt to a character, similar to the Damage Immunity status effect in . Additionally, it prevents damage over time effects (such as Bleed) from taking hold, so long as the damage nullification remains active after the hit. While a player character has the Armor Veil buff, their health bar (regardless of the HP they have) will be tinted dark blue. This does not apply if the character merely stands in a field granting the buff.

Attack Up is a Status Effect in and . It temporarily increases the character's damage dealt. The damage increase is additive with most other damage-enhancing effects in the game, such as accessories that increase damage dealt under certain conditions.

Art Follow-Up is a Status Effect in . It deals flat damage equal to 2 times the attack stat of the person who set the Field, whenever someone uses an Art in the field. It also ignores any enemy damage reduction.

The Aurora Shelf (Japanese: , Amaneseru Kōgen, Amanecer Plateau) is an area in , located in the Cent-Omnia Region. The remains of the Bionis' Leg and the Kingdom of Tantal make up this area, with there also being ruins present from Satorl Marsh, Makna Forest, and the Bionis' Shoulder.
Atattra's Rampart (Japanese: , Attatera Kyoheki) is a landmark in . It is located in Vermilion Woods.
This page lists all the quests available on the Aurora Shelf.
The Atattra Access Elevator (Japanese: , Attatera-dō Renraku-yō Shōkōki) is a location in , located on the Aurora Shelf. It connects to the Elevator, Upper Landing.
Art Unlock Kits are Key Items in . They can be used to unlock Art slots for the party. There are twelve of them in total in the Cent-Omnia Region.
Aspar Eggs are Normal Enemies in . They are Eggs that hatch into Baby Aspars, and can be found at level 16 near the Pioneer's Camp on the Aurora Shelf. When defeated, they drop common Hard Eggshells.
This page lists all the collectopaedia entries for the Aurora Shelf. When filling in an entry, 6-7 Affinity Points will be rewarded.
This page lists all the Enemypaedia entries for enemies on the Aurora Shelf.
Atu Ignas are Quest Exclusive Bosses in . They are members of the Igna family that are fought at level 22 in the Exile Fortress Ruins on the Aurora Shelf during Riku's Workshop.
Aromatic Anlood Meats are items in . They can be dropped by Rudoni Anloods on the Aurora Shelf.

Auresco, Royal Capital/Night is a track from , composed by Manami Kiyota. It is track eight of the Xenoblade 2: Torna ~ The Golden Country Original Soundtrack, and track eight of disc eleven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays at night in Auresco.

At Our Life's End is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track one of disc nine from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track one of disc twenty from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It is a piano arrangement of Future Awaits. This song plays on the title screen for . Na'el also plays it on the piano in The Ark, where it serves as the area theme after the cutscene "Klaus's World".

Arts Coins are a game mechanic in . They can be exchanged at the Arts Manual Shop for Advanced Art books for Shulk, Melia, Kino, and Nene. Each art book costs one Arts Coin. Arts Coins can be obtained when defeating any Unique Monster or Fogbeast (excluding any Story Exclusive Fogbeasts) for the first time. Additionally, upon killing the same Fogbeast any additional time, the party has a 10% chance of obtaining an additional Arts Coin.

The Arts Manual Shop is a shop in . It is initially located at Companions' Cape on the Bionis' Shoulder, later relocating to Gran Dell after the Companions return there. This shop sells Advanced Art books for Shulk, Melia, Kino, and Nene for one Arts Coin each.
Attack Familivs are Story Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Familiv family, and can be found at level 59 inside the Tower of Eternity on Volitaris after being summoned by Void.
Arthem is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian who can be found at the Waypoint Market in the Kingdom of Uraya during Sniff out the Spy, during which he is one of the three spy suspects.
Asghal is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian who can be found at Goetuis Wharf #1 in the Indoline Praetorium during Bana the Schemer.

Aunt Corinne's House is a shop in . It can be found in Corinne's House in the Leftherian Archipelago. Corinne allows the party to rest here as though it were an inn. Corinne initially offers to let the party rest here free of charge, but due to Rex's insistence, she charges the party 1 G to rest here.

The Battle of Sword Valley was an important event that took place one year prior to the events of . It is during this battle that the player (who controls Dunban during this section of the game) learns how to use the Monado. This event is the prologue of .

Batubatu (Japanese: , Barudo) is a Nopon in . He is a traveler, alongside Gerugu, although he often tries to do things alone which end up badly. Pepa is his niece. He can be found at Traveller's Rest on Bionis' Leg.

Bana (Japanese: , Bān) is a Nopon in . He can be found in the southeast area of the Central Plaza in Frontier Village. It is later revealed that he is the real kingpin of the secret organization involving making food and drinks out of Red Pollen Orbs and selling them to the Secret Club in Alcamoth. He also appears in under the fake name, Bama, at the Grand Arch on the Bionis' Shoulder.

Azure Hollyhocks (Japanese: , Shīburūsuton ) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Mechonis Field and Colony 6. They can be traded for with Scarlen in Satorl Marsh after the events of Mechonis Core. According to their description, they are beautiful flowers that are also known as sea-blue stones. Two are required for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 11,000 Noponstones.

Baroba (Japanese: , Baroru) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. He can be found at the Main Entrance of Alcamoth between 06:00 and 18:00 and, after the events at Mechonis Core, just west of the Nopon Tower in Frontier Village.

Azure Mice (Japanese: , Azuraitoppo) are collectables in . They can be found in Bionis' Interior. According to their description, they are stocky mice that are indigo in colour and move in extreme slow motion.

※ After this quest is completed, Leku may offer another quest. See Popularity Premonition. After this and story An Errand for the Heropon are completed, Modamo may offer another quest. See Lousy Lizards. Beat Kilaki to it! (Japanese: , Kika yori Sakimawari) is a quest in . It can be received from Leku in the upper area of the Archaeology Level in Frontier Village. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

Avenge a Mamapon's Death (Japanese: , Haha no Shi wo Koete) is a quest in . It can be received from Rasha in the Central Plaza of Frontier Village with Sharla in the lead of the party. She can be found firstly on the southeast border of Sacred Altar's pool then at the Armour Shop. After this quest is completed, Sharla's Reliance skill branch will be unlocked.

Awakening is an Aura used by some enemies in and that, while in effect, increases that enemy's level. Most enemies tend to activate this aura when their HP is at least under 50% of its max and the aura also has different durations depending on the enemy using it, although it rarely lasts for very long. Like all auras, the enemy using it will appear to have mist surrounding it while it is active, with Awakening having blue mist.

The Barren Moor (Japanese: , Kyomu no Shitsugen) is a location in . It is located in Satorl Marsh, directly south of the Altar of Fate, and directly north of the Silent Obelisk. Many enemies can be found roaming the area, including the Sunlight Schvaik, Officer Volffs, Satorl Volffs, Green Feris and Coppice and Grove Quadwings.
Back Atk Plus (Japanese: , Haimen Kōgeki Kyōka) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that increases damage when attacking enemies from behind. __TOC__

Beach Krabbles (Japanese: , Bīchi Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family, and can be found in Colony 9 along the shoreline south of Anti-Air Battery 1 and along the shores of Cliff Lake. Three of them need to be defeated to complete Monster Quest 3 - Part 2, and they can drop Small Shells, which are required for Material Quest 1.
Battle Gear (Japanese: , Batoru Gia) is medium head armour in . It is worn by Homs soldiers when they are training. They can be bought at the Ether Light Shop at Colony 9.
Battle Armour is medium torso armour in . It is worn by Homs soldiers when they train.
Battle Gauntlets are medium arms armour in . They can be dropped by Little Skeeters. They are worn by Homs soldiers during their training.
Battle Leggings are medium legs armour in . They are worn by Homs soldiers when they are training.
Battle Boots are medium feet armour in . They are worn by Homs soldiers when they train.

Bask Cave Passage (Japanese: , Bagusu Gankutsu-dōri) is a landmark in . It is located on the upper level of Bionis' Leg. It is a cave passage located south of Kasharpa Falls, which leads to Colony 6. It is accessed by crossing some bridges over the water around Kasharpa Falls, where the party can swim.

Battle Soul (Japanese: , Batoru Souru) is one of Shulk's supporting arts in and . It sacrifices half of Shulk's current HP in order to fill his Talent Gauge by a certain amount. The amount the talent gauge is filled depends on the art's level.

Battling Brutes (Japanese: , Butsukariau Futatsu) is a quest in . It can be received by Dulland lying northwest of the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg, after the events at Mechonis Core, after completing A Flower for a Rose and with Fiora in the lead. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment.
The Battle Driver (Japanese: , Batorubankā) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn. It is not dropped by any enemies, but can be bought or traded for.

Barrier Gnashers (Japanese: , Shōheki no Tsukutsuku) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Biters wielded by Riki. They can be acquired by trading with Orkatix who can be found on the Fallen Arm and they can also be obtained as a quest reward.

Autumn Staves (Japanese: , Komorebi no Tsue, Staff of Dappled Sunlight) are weapons in . They are staves wielded by Melia, and can be obtained from the gold Treasure Chests of various mid-level enemies. Autumn Staves are also available for purchase in Colony 6 and trade.

Bafalgar Tomb (Japanese: , Barufaruga Bochi) is a Secret Area in . It is located in Tephra Cave. It is here that Shura is met, who gives the party a series of quests — The Book, The Blood, The Path, The Coffin and The Gratitude of Bafalgar. It can only be accessed after completing the Mechonis Core. There are two hidden rooms; one behind the Sacrificial Altar and another on the left wall while descending the stairs from the altar. They are unlocked after completing certain quests: * The hidden wall behind the altar is revealed after completing The Blood of Bafalgar. It will lead to a corridor and at the end of the corridor where a quest item, the Ancient Lily, can be found. It is requi

The Basin Cave (Japanese: , Suiban no Dōkutsu) is a location in . It is located in Satorl Marsh, just west of the Sororal Statues, and can only be accessed through a small cave entrance in the water near the Statues. The White Radiant, necessary for Ancient Ceremony Offerings, can be found here, as can several Storm Vangs.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Back Pain (Japanese: , Yōtsūmochi wa Taihen da) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Galdo after speaking with Lar'shen, both of whom can be found at the base of the stairs in Alcamoth's Great Hall at night. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Balanced Palamedes (Japanese: , Tenbin no Paromidesu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 62 in Central Factory together with two Offensive/DIARY, just northwest of the Central Tower Roof on the third floor (on the ground level under the narrow elevated walkway). It can drop the Reinforced Jets required for Best Boots.

Basin Antols (Japanese: , Beisun Antoru) are enemies in . They are members of the Antol family, and can be found at level 16 on path to Daksha Shrine and outside the Refugee Camp. Two of them must be defeated to complete Bionis' Leg's Monster Quest 2.

Bagrus Nebulae are enemies in . They are members of the Nebula family, and they can be found at level 96 near the Waypoint Beacon landmark in Makna Forest, or in place of the Caris Nebula if a heat wave is occurring. Bagrus Nebulae disappear altogether if it is raining.

Azure Flamii Wings are rare materials in . They can only be dropped by one species of Flamii in Colony 9 and are not available for trade. According to their description, they are vivid wings coloured like a clear blue sky. Two of them are required for Birthday Shoes.

Baelzeb Gogols (Japanese: , Beruzebu Gogōru) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 84 near the Soter Ruins in Satorl Marsh. They can drop the Gogol Horns needed for A Token of Friendship and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Baelfael Gogols (Japanese: , Beruferu Gogōru) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 82 in Satorl Marsh near the Soter Ruins. A group of them is located near the Unique Monster named Indomitable Daulton. They can drop the Gogol Horns needed for A Token of Friendship and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Balgas (Japanese: , Barukasu) are a family of rare horned quadrupedal enemies in the . Balgas are similar in appearance to Ories. Like Ories, they resemble bulls or yaks, although there is no equivalent to Aries. There is a minor appearance change between games; in they have glowing blue and purple lines, whereas in and they do not.

Battle Eye (Japanese: , Ikusagan) is one of Dunban's arts in . It activates an aura that may inflict Lock-On to a target. It also increases Dunban's double attack rate by 25% and his talent gauge by 5% for every attack dodged while the aura remains active.

Barbaro Ignas are enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 27 near Exile Fortress in the Satorl Marsh. They can drop the Igna Stone Pots needed for Nopon Determination.

Azul Andos (Japanese: , Asūru Andosu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Andos family, and can be found at level 35 in the High Entia Tomb. They are the only enemy that can drop the Andos Antennae needed for Collect Quest 2. They can also drop the New Cylinders needed for Restoring the Capital 2.

BLADE Tower (Japanese: , Bureido Tawā) is a landmark in . It is located in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. It seems to be a location for Maurice to speak. While there is not an announcement on the screen of the tower, a percentage is shown. The inside of the tower serves as a headquarters for BLADE. Though the player cannot regularly enter the tower, there are certain missions that allow the party to be in the tower for a brief amount of time.

Bastion Warrior (known as Heavy Striker in the Japanese version) is a Class featured in . It is one of six final classes and can only be leveled up from Shield Trooper. The Bastion Warrior receives greatly increased HP and Melee Attack but reduced Potential, and has four Skill slots. Mastering this class enables Cross to equip Gatling Guns and Shields with any class.

Beach Forfexes (Japanese: , Bīchi Pagurusu) are normal enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 4-9 on the coasts of Primordia. A large number of them can be found at FN Site 107 at any time, and at Cliffside Beach during the day. They drop Broken Pincers, five of which are needed for the mission Skell Repair: Balancer.

Azure Lagoon (Japanese: , Burū Hōru, Blue Hole) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, under the Barbarich Desert and reachable from FN Site 313. As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("The Deep Trench of Azure Lagoon").

Baby Armus (Japanese: , Bebī Aruma) are enemies in . They are members of the Armu family, and appear at the south of Anti-Air Battery 1 in Colony 9. They are approximately level 8 - 10. They drop Treasure Chests. To complete Colony 9's Monster Quest 2 - Part 2, one of the level 8 Baby Armus near Anti-Air Battery 1 must be defeated. They are also the only enemies that drop Fresh Armu Milk, which is required for one route of Overworked and Underpaid.

The BLADE Scout is a game mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles X. The BLADE Scout menu is available on the BLADE Scout Console at the BLADE Concourse in New Los Angeles. It allows players to scout other players' Avatars. This mechanic was discontinued with the shutdown of Wii U online services but is available year later in the on the Nintendo Switch.

The BLADE Report was a Network tool in . This feature has been discontinued. It was used to communicate with the Squad's players and exchange information with them. By progressing through the game within a Squad, a member could submit a report and share information with all the members such as a Treasure Box found, a new area, or a particular enemy. Previous, even old reports stored on the server might be received later. After a battle, Squad players could leave items to other players, a menu proposes to "Takes all", "Select and Take", "Sell all", or a Treasure Deal.
Beam Bomber is one of Mia's two Signature Arts in . It is acquired as a reward for completing the Affinity Mission Mia Grows Up.

The BLADE Barracks (Japanese: , Bureido Hōmu) is a region in . It is located in New Los Angeles and is accessible from the eponymous landmark in the Administrative District. BLADE Barracks corresponds to the BLADE home. The Barracks accessed in-game is the one issued to Elma, which she shares with Cross, Lin, and Tatsu.
The Barracks Interior (Japanese: , Bureido Hōmu Naibu) is a landmark in . It is located in the BLADE Barracks of New Los Angeles.

BLADE Concourse (Japanese: , Bureido Konkōsu) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. The Mission Control and BLADE Scout Console are both located here.

BLADE Level is an important mechanic in . It displays the party's experience level within the BLADE organization, and can be raised by earning Division Points. Raising the BLADE Level unlocks more Basic Missions and increases the maximum number of Reward Tickets the party can have. In addition, Cross can speak to Eleonora to unlock new customization features for the BLADE Barracks, and to increase his/her Archaeological, Biological, or Mechanical Field-Skill level, which allows access to more Treasure Boxes and FrontierNav Sites. BLADE Level is absent from .

BLADE Level Basics (Japanese: , Bureido Reberu wo Manabu) is a Normal Mission in . It can be received from Eleonora at the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. It is required in order to start Chapter 4. This is the only Normal Mission that is absent in , due to the removal of BLADE Level.

Barista Court (Japanese: , Rate Avenyū, Latte Avenue) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles. It starts from Melville Street between its center and western end and extends northwards.

The Barbarich Desert (Japanese: , Ibittsa Sabaku, Ibizza Desert) is a landmark in . It is located in Oblivia, east of the Leaning Ring. There is a river which drains into the Azure Lagoon just to the east.
Balance Breaker is a Melee Art and one of Lao's two unique Arts in . Cross learns it after completing A Friend in Need.

Bacchanal Scirpos (Japanese: , Bakkasu Shirunea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Scirpos and can be found at level 24-28 at Stoyanov Trail, southeast of FN Site 312, at Leaning Ring, and at Central Ibra Ravine in Oblivia.

Barnabas, the Despot (Japanese: , Bōkun Barunabāshu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Vigent and can be found during the day at level 65 on Oblivia's Aaroy Plain. It spawns by the Cliffside Camp and runs in a large loop between the river and the Yawning Giant, and can be seen from anywhere within this area. It must be defeated for the eponymous Basic Mission Barnabas, the Despot.

BFFs (Japanese: , Nopon Yūkōjōyaku, The Nopon Friendship Treaty) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be received from inside the BLADE Barracks and the primary destinations are Noctilum and Oblivia. 30,000 Credits are needed to complete this mission.
Badr Basin (Japanese: , Baderu Bonchi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, north of the South Cinderdunes.
Badr Stronghold (Japanese: , Baderu Yōsai) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, on the north side of the Badr Stonebridge. It is a Ganglion base.

Bandits' Refuge (Japanese: , Tōzoku no Negura) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Cauldros, and can be reached by following a small sidepath on the eastern Adder Byroad. It is usually uninhabited, however is used by Fraisie and the Avatar of God as a hideaway during Rites of Ruin. As with all Unexplored Territories, its discovery yields an achievement ("Scouting Bandits' Refuge").

Ball Mosquitoes (Japanese: , Bōrumosukīto) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can appear anywhere in Primordia, but are most common in caves. Ten of them are needed to complete the mission Bloodsuckers.
The Badr Stonebridge (Japanese: , Baderu no Iwabashi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, spanning over Badr Basin.
Bates is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is located at Division Drive in the Administrative District.

Basic Probes are types of Data Probes in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are the default and most basic probes amongst the different types of data probes, being automatically installed when a FrontierNav Site is first claimed. Basic Probes generate Miranium and Revenue yields at 50% efficiency.

Balance Rock (Japanese: , Baransu Rokku) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in southeastern Oblivia. Its main feature is the huge tooth-shaped boulder precariously balanced on a slope.

Beachside Trove (Japanese: , Umibe no Oana) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cave located on Oblivia's South Coast near FN Site 317 or directly northwest of FN Site 319. The entrance to the cave is hidden behind a large rock pillar. The cave consists of an outer chamber containing one Collectible, and an inner chamber containing 39 more Collectibles and a Treasure Box (Mechanical Level 5). As with all Unexplored Territories, its discovery merits an achievement ("Relaxing at Beachside Trove").
Babaco Leaves (Japanese: , Hababakō) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum. Twelve of them are needed for No Friends Like Nopon.

Bananaleaves (Japanese: , Rīfubanana) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, near the southern part of Canopied Nightwood. Five are needed for Bananaleaf Bonanza.

Beagflea Squashes (Japanese: , Gi Dou Kabocha) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia. Three are required for Proficiency Exam 5, which is required to earn a Skell.

Beaporges (Japanese: , Beapōji) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum, in particular near FN Site 407. They must be collected 2 times as one of the Squad Tasks for BLADE Mission No. 14.
Baibai Beetles (Japanese: , Sayonarakanabun) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
Autoposturizers (Japanese: , Ōtoposuchā) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros.

Beasts' Lair (Japanese: , Yajū no Su) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, directly north of New Los Angeles. This large cave contains a pack of Lawless Grexes and rarely sphinxes. Dieter, the Epicure runs down to the cave's entrance, but will not enter.

Baabara, the Evangelical (Japanese: , Fukuin no Mei, lit. Gospel May) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Ovis family. It can be found at level 12 in Primordia during the day at South Janpath Plain, east of South Janpath BC, surrounded by a flock of Docile Ovis.

Bart is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is initially found at West Gate Plain in Primordia, near the West Gate of New Los Angeles, during the Affinity Mission The Repair Job. Once the mission is completed, he can later be found in the Hangar of the Administrative District near the Restricted Hangar Entrance.

Banshee Cave (Japanese: , Kikoku no Dōkutsu) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cave located in Sylvalum, north of FN Site 407. The entrance is a short distance directly west of FN Site 407, guarded by two Titanium Oc-servs. The cave is large enough for Skells. It is visited during the normal mission Unknown Assailant.

Balduino, the Wicked-Eyed (Japanese: , Angan no Baruduino) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Aeviter family. It can be found at level 89 at Sentinel's Nest in Noctilum, guarding a crashed helicopter. It is dormant, like the nearby Crazed Aeviters.

Bartley, the Conflagration (Japanese: , Gōka no Bātore) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Gerrid family. It can be found at level 31 below the Adder Byroad in Cauldros. It constantly jumps up and down alongside two Bluff Gerrids.

Badul, the One-Eyed (Japanese: , Sekigan no Baduru) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Milsaadi Ganglion member. He can be found at level 46 in the daytime in Sylvalum, on the roof of a building in the southwest corner of Hilal Stronghold. He will drop down when the alien container is approached.

Badul's Seidr (Japanese: , Baduru Sen'yō Basugia) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Ganglion Seidr machine. It can be found at level 61 at Cavernous Abyss in Sylvalum during nighttime. It is the Seidr of Badul, the One-Eyed. It appears on a ledge above the western side of the abyss.

Awakened Liceors (Japanese: , Aweiku Kurāra) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Liceor family, and can be found at level 41-47 in Sylvalum near FN Site 413 and around a Sand Aeviter near FN Site 415 during rising energy mists. They replace the Dazzling Liceors normally found there.

Azure Blattas (Japanese: , Ajūru Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 57-58 in the northeast corner of the Abyss Reservoir in Sylvalum during the day.
Background Noise is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Commando at rank 5. Cross, Elma, and Phog can use this skill.
Autosentries (Japanese: , Gādomashin, lit. Guard Machine) are machine enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. There are only two types and they are both Mission Exclusive Enemies.

The Autosentry Mk. II (Japanese: , Gādo Mashin TypeB) is Mission Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is an Autosentry machine, and is fought at level 60 at the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles during the fifth battle of The Gauntlet.
Avaricious Shrads (Japanese: , Gurīdo Zuttā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Shrad machines, and can be found at level 52 at Anvil Rock One in Sylvalum.

The BLADE Snipers (Japanese: , Bureido Sunaipā) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are level 17 BLADE members working with Gadd, and must be fought during two Normal Missions: * During Mystery Man three of them are encountered at Noctilum's Waterway Tangle. * During Professorial three of them are encountered at Sylvalum's North Cinderdunes and must be defeated within 10 minutes.
Beam Boost is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Enforcer at rank 4. Cross, Doug, Yelv, and Mia can use this skill.
Beam Guard is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Enforcer at rank 6.

BLADE Missions were an online gameplay mechanic in . They were made up of Squad Tasks and Squad Missions, and were randomly assigned to the player's Squad during normal gameplay. By completing them, players could earn Reward Tickets, BLADE Medals, Credits, Experience Points, and Battle Points. The mechanic was discontinued with shutdown of Wii U online services. This mechanic returned in .
Barbed Queen Qmoevas (Japanese: , Taronkuīn Kumūba) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Qmoeva machines, and can be found at level 50 below a ledge south of FN Site 504 in Cauldros.

Barbed Rook Qmoevas (Japanese: , Taronrūku Kumūba) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Qmoeva machines, and can be found dormant at level 36 around the Ganglion encampment at the Abandoned Bivouac in Cauldros. Three must be defeated during Arms Testers Wanted.

The BLADE Trooper (Japanese: , Bureido Torūpā) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a BLADE member, and can be found at level 17 at Middle Hushflood in Noctilum. Defeating her is required during the Affinity Mission My Dream.

Backup Request is a Basic Mission in . It is a request from Phog at the Water Purification Plant in the Residential District and the primary destination is New Los Angeles. This mission must be accepted in order to start the Affinity Mission Foggy Dilemma.

Avatar of God is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She appears during Rites of Ruin after speaking to Fraisie, and looks exactly like Fraisie. She is then revealed to be TW772: Trinn in disguise. The default icon remains displayed on the Affinity Chart after completing the mission, there is no dedicated portrait for this NPC.

Bazis Wolfen (Japanese: , Bajishi Urufen) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Prone of the Tree Clan, and can be found in the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles at night. He is Hexuna Nebra's husband.
Axing Falsaxum is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Interceptors and the primary destination is Oblivia.
Bananaleaf Bonanza is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a café manager and the primary destination is Noctilum.
The Barrage-Cloak is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X.
Azure Sacrifole Feathers are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from the heads of blue Sacrifoles in Sylvalum. They are components for Overdrive.APPEND-HP augments.

The BLADE Soldier (Japanese: , Bureido Sorujā) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a BLADE member, and can be found at level 28 atop the Headwater Summit in Primordia. Defeating him is required during the Normal Mission Alien Nation.
Avi (Japanese: , Avi) is a Human NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found south of the Repenta Diner in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles.
Balaena A is a Holofigure in . It depicts a purple Balaena variant. It can be obtained from Draken, the Drifting Cloud at Primordia Waters.
Balaena B is a Holofigure in . It depicts a blue balaena variant. It can be obtained from Rajidi, the Cumuliform in Primordia.

Barrel Tosser is a special Holofigure in . It depicts a Cavern Clan Prone throwing a barrel, with two more barrels beside him. It is otained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Art of War.
Barrel Dodger is a special Holofigure in . It depicts a Nopon jumping over a barrel involved during Hair Apparent. It is obtained as a reward for completing this Normal Mission.
Barreled Over is a special Holofigure in . It depicts a Nopon being hit by a barrel. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Special Delivery.

Balancing the Ether is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.10, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting four Vendura's Galdrs. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Bargain Tank Tops are casual torso Armors made by Sakuraba Industries in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are available through several missions. All colors in this set have the same stats.

BLADE Extraction is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.18, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty-six Sacrifoles. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Bargain Turtlenecks are casual upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are produced by Sakuraba Industries.
Beam Res Up is a ground armor attribute resistance Augment in and that increases beam attribute resistance. The Skell equivalent is SpecUp.BEAM-RES.
Beam Attack Plus is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that increases the damage dealt by all beam-attribute weapons and Arts. The Skell equivalent is AttributeDmg.BEAM.
Back Attack Plus is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that increases damage dealt when attacking from behind an enemy. The Skell equivalent is PositionDmg.BACK.
Beamsabers are spare weapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from white Puges or Viragos.
Beam Res Down is a stat debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Beam Res Down increases the damage taken from beam-attribute attacks.

The BLACK-ROD is a Skell Weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained as a reward for completing the Time Attack Mission Twin Dolls of Mystery, or extremely more rarely as a reward for completing the Squad Mission The Unknown Threat. It is the rod of Neilnail Furvus.

BLADE Wear is a type of Armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This class of armor is primarily made by Sakuraba Industries, though an unknown manufacturer produces a series that can only be obtained through crafting. BLADE Wear offers comparable defense to Light Wear but with lessened resistance.
Beam Resistance is a stat in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It displays resistance to beam-type attacks.
B-Centipedes are sidearms for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Titan Missile type Galdrs, Gularth or Sylooth.
|-|XM230 Model= |-|XM250 Model= |-|XXM240 Model= |-|XXM250 Model= B-Claws are sidearms for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Cetos, Tornado Claw type Galdrs or black Puges.
|-|XXR240 Model= |-|XXR260 Model= B-Rifles are sidearms for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Titan Missile type Galdrs, Gularth or Sylooth.
Backbombs are back weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Almandal, Millepods, Purgovents or Fuse Blower type Seidrs.
BB-Swords are back weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Viragos or white Puges.
B-Gatlings are back weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from They can be obtained from Titan Missile type Galdrs, Gularth or Sylooth.
B2-Gatlings are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from white Marnucks, M-Laser/Spine-Cannon/E-Bubble/B-Bomb types Qmoevas.
B-Snipers are weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Titan Missile type Galdrs, Gularth or Sylooth.
BLADE Pants are Casual Wear leg armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Bargain Jeans are Casual Wear leg armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Bargain Shorts are Casual Wear leg armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Bargain Trousers are Casual Wear leg armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Barrier is a buff in . A barrier is created around the character that absorbs a certain amount of damage from all attacks inflicted.
Beam Attack Down is a debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It reduces beam attack damage.
Aware is an enemy-exclusive aura in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This aura grants an effect specific to the Art that activates it. These effects tend to be offensive in nature.
Bargain Hoodies are Casual Wear upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Bargain Jackets are Casual Wear upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Bargain Tees are Casual Wear upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Back Slash (Japanese: , Bakku Surasshu) is one of Shulk's physical arts in and . When the enemy is hit from behind, Back Slash inflicts double damage.

Battle Arts are battle mechanics in and . They are techniques that behave differently from an Auto-Attack and must be activated manually. Usage of Battle Arts is restricted by the cooldown mechanic; once a Battle Art has been used, it cannot be used again until a certain length of time has passed or a specific condition is met. Each Battle Art has a unique set of properties that may include dealing higher damage, granting status buffs to allies or status debuffs to enemies, healing party members, or drawing aggro. Their effects can be executed upon activation or be context sensitive (such as Arts that require specific positioning). In , arts with a conditional bonus effect will be highlighte
Axe Twist (Japanese: , Sukuryūakkusu Lit. "Screw Axe") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using a Greataxe.
Bear Smash (Japanese: , Beāsumasshu) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Nia's arts when using a Greataxe.
Baroon Armu (Japanese: , Bāren Aruma) are enemies in . They are members of the Armu family, and can be found at level 26-28 at the Chansagh Wastes of the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Bana's Bedroom (Japanese: , Bān no Shinshitsu) is a Landmark in . It is located in Goldmouth in the Argentum Trade Guild. It is the bedroom of Chairman Bana. Niranira can be found here during the Quest Bana's Secret Treasure. It also contains a white Treasure Trove and a red barrel.

The Ballast Disposal Chute (Japanese: , Barasuto Haishutsukuchi) is a landmark in . It is located on the Titan Battleship in the Gormott Province, and leads between the Treetop Path and the Cloud Tank Chamber. There are no enemies here.

Battle Command (Japanese: , Sentō Shikijo) is a location in . It is located on the Titan Battleship in the Gormott Province, beyond the Bridge and leading to the Hangar Passage and Starboard Balcony. There is a Treasure Trove here.
The Ayvill Shopping District (Japanese: , Aiviru Shōgyō-ku) is a Location in . It is located in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Badfella's Cave Fort (Japanese: , Zainin no Gankutsu Toride) is a location in . It is located in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya, in a cave south-east of Tardy Gate. It is an Igna hideaway containing many high-level enemies. There is a Treasure Trove here, and Budada can be found here during the DLC quest M.I.A. Nopon.

Battlescar Cove (Japanese: , Senshō no Irie) is a Landmark in . It is located on the Peninsula of Temperantia, and is the first place visited on Temperantia. There are two fish Collection Points, one Treasure Trove, a Salvage Point, and the NPC Timur here. A path leads directly to Bardina Plateau. There are no enemies here.
Bardina Plateau (Japanese: , Barudina Kōchi) is a location in . It is located on the Peninsula of Temperantia, just beyond Battlescar Cove, and must be crossed to reach Overlook Hill.

Balquors Ruins (Japanese: , Barukurusu Iseki) is a landmark in . It is located on the Upper Level of the Cliffs of Morytha, between the Fallen-Down Pilgrim's Way and Cape O-uru. There is a Salvage point here. Neyaya of the Twelve Brothersisterpon can be found here after Chapter 7.
The Ayvill Shopping Dist., Roof (Japanese: , Aiviru Shōgyō-ku - Okujō) is a Landmark in . It is located in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

The Bastion of Varrac (Japanese: , Varaku Honjin) is a location in . It is located on the Central Plain of Temperantia, just west of Toxbloom Spring, and can most easily be reached by navigating across the toxic water.

Beat Paste Parathas are Staple Food Pouch items in . They can be purchased at Tilly Bakery in Torigoth in the Gormott Province. They can also be purchased for 1,200 G from the Pouch Item Emporium in the Land of Challenge after collecting the Nopon Invitation, Pt. 2 on Version 1.5.2 or later.
The Bassani Deeds are Store Deed key items in . They can be purchased from Bassani Butchers in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Bagna Oyster Rolls are Seafood Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Tatraty Fish in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. One of them is required to unlock Fiora's level 2 "Ichthyology" Field Skill.
Baked Narcipears are Dessert Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Placks Patisserie in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.
Bassani Butchers is a shop in . It is run by Sketach and can be found in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain. This shop specializes in Meats.

Bagoan Sovereigns (Japanese: , Bagōn Roiyaru) are enemies in . They are Kustal-type Sovereigns that can be found at level 49-55 in the Land of Morytha. One is in the middle floor of the Fallen Skyscraper, four are on Highway 8. Five must be defeated to unlock Aegaeon's and Praxis' level 3 "Water Mastery", and Perun's level 3 "Ice Mastery" Field Skills, as well as Roc's level 5 Feather Typhoon on their affinity charts.

Azure Reginald (Japanese: , Sōten no Regiosu) is a Unique Monster in . He is a member of the Lexos family and can be found at level 41 in the Coralline Sanctum, near the Crown of Sanctuary in the Kingdom of Uraya, except during Night Incense weather. He must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 3 Ascension Blade on her affinity chart.

Beast-Hunter William (Japanese: , Shishigari no Virumu) is a Unique Monster in . He is a Driver enemy, and can be found at level 99 at the Olethro Playhouse in the Kingdom of Uraya, during the Final Chapter and after completing the quest Farewell, Good Friend.

Autumn-Shower Melvin (Japanese: , Akisame no Kashirudo) is a Unique Monster in . He is a Driver enemy, and can be found at level 46 at Lumos Pillar in the Kingdom of Tantal at night after his brother, Spring-Shower Elliott, has been defeated and has dropped the Letter to Melvin. Melvin appears sitting by Elliott's Tombstone and is fought further up the pillar.

Bearing Her Soul (Japanese: , Nanakoori no Chōsen, Ursula's Challenge) is a Blade Quest in . It can be received from Kiara at Abble's Fountain after finishing the "Not Quite Comfortable Yet" Heart-to-Heart. It is Ursula's exclusive Blade Quest, used to unlock further levels of her Affinity Chart's Key Affinity.

Bafoo Crustips (Japanese: , Bafūn Shuribu) are enemies in . They are members of the Crustip family and can be found at level 29-31 on the Fief of Forgetfulness during clear weather, and the Chansagh Wastes in the Empire of Mor Ardain when there is no storm. Five of them must be defeated to unlock Pyra's level 3 Prominence Revolt on her affinity chart.
Barcan is an NPC in . Barcan is a Leftherian who can be found in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago. Barcan runs a shop called Coral Leaf Fresh Fish specialized in Seafood.

Bamboo Seeds are Tree collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Uraya, in particular at the Cataracts of Rujah. One can be used to prepare a ration needed for the quest The Supply Situation.

Beat Shrimps are Fish collectibles in . They can be found in the Leftherian Archipelago, in particular from the Collection Points located on Baldotas Isle, in Lud Cloudway beside a huge pile of dark rocks near Epicurean Ligia's tombstone, and in Orl Cloudway: Rigitte, the third one from the Skip Travel point. In the , Beat Shrimps can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo. Four are required to cook Pyra's Baked Redfish and five to cook Meatball Pot-au-Feu at Tora's House or Corinne's House after obtaining the Fire Dragons Recipe from the DLC Quest Midnight Feasting.
Bauz Eks (Japanese: , Bōzu Ekusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Eks family, and can be found at level 35-40 at the Titan Weapon Dig Site on the Central Plain of Temperantia.
Bagis Ignas (Japanese: , Bāgesuto Igūna) are enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 47-52 at the Bastion of Varrac on the Central Plain of Temperantia.
Beat Ignas (Japanese: , Bīto Igūna) are enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 47-52 at the Bastion of Varrac on the Central Plain of Temperantia.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Avant-Garde Medals (Japanese: , Abangyarudo Medaru) are accessories in . They provide special healing, restoring the wearer's HP by up to 22% of the damage inflicted with each Critical Hit. They are the upgraded version of the Classic Medal and Modern Medal accessories.

Azure Striker, Form the Second: Hellfire (Japanese: ), abbreviated Azure II: Hellfire, is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Whipswords. When used, Mòrag raises her whipswords then does a horizontal lash at her enemy.

Azure Striker, Form the Second: Judgment (Japanese: ), abbreviated Azure II: Judgment, is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Whipswords. When used, Mòrag moves her whipsword and lashes it while also evading enemy attacks.

Azure Striker, Form the Second: Radiance (Japanese: , Sōenken Nii no Kata Myōō), abbreviated Azure II: Radiance, is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Whipswords. When used, Mòrag first does an upward lash with her right whipsword, then another with her left whipsword, then finishes with a jumping downward slash releasing blue fire on her enemy.

Azure Striker, Form the Second: Blaze (Japanese: ), abbreviated Azure II: Blaze, is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Whipswords. When used, Mòrag cross swipes her whipswords at the enemy.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Beast Hoods (Japanese: , Bīsuto Fūdo) are accessories in and . They increase the rate of aggro reduction from taking damage and aggro lowering effects by up to 22%. The Camo Hood, Skeleton Hood and Vanish Hood accessories offer stronger instances of this equipment's effect.
Battle Top (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using the Shield Hammer.
Bamboo Sword Smithy is a shop in . It is run by Nubnub and can be found in the Cliffs of Morytha's Inlet. It is specialized in Core Chips.

Axion Chips are Core Chips in . They can be obtained from Treasure Troves in the World Tree and the Land of Morytha, dropped by several enemies, and rewarded for completion of several Challenge Battle Mode challenges. Axiom Chips share their appearance with Dark Matter Chips and Mirror Matter Chips. __TOC__

Battery Chips are Core Chips in and . They can be purchased at the Casheefs Blacksmiths shop in the Kingdom of Tantal, and in are rewarded upon completion of Azurda SOS and dropped by Xane Pippitos. Battery Chips share their appearance with Booster Chips, Engine Chips, and Motor Chips. __TOC__
Barz Gyannas (Japanese: , Bāsuto Gyanomu) are enemies in . They are members of the Gyanna family, and can be found at level 32-34 at Valdorm's Mound in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Avys Quadwings (Japanese: , Abisu Kurōdo) are enemies in . They are members of the Quadwing family, and can be found at level 28-34 on Daram Isle in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Aybam Medoozes (Japanese: , Ēbamu Jerī) are enemies in . They are members of the Medooz family, and can be found at level 32 - 36 at the Orl Cloudway: Rigitte in the Leftherian Archipelago. Five of them must be defeated to unlock Gorg's level 3 "FAS", and Azami's level 3 Nightmare Rondeau on their affinity charts.
Badile is an NPC in . Badile is an Ardainian who can be found at the Admar Storage Zone in the Empire of Mor Ardain during Fool's Gold.

The Beastly Core Crystal is a special Core Crystal in . It allows the party to awake Wulfric and is obtained from the Elder Arachno, however, it cannot be used until after the events at the Brigands' Hideout.
Back Attack is an Info Item in . It can be purchased from the Informant shop in the Argentum Trade Guild.
Bana's Secret Treasure is a quest in . It can be received from Niranira in Bana's Bedroom in the Argentum Trade Guild.

Beast-type enemies belong to the following enemy species: Ageshu, Anlood, Ardainian Rotts, Ardun, Aries, Armu, Aspar, Behemoth, Brionac Madadh, Bufa, Buloofo, Bunnit, Camill, Eks, Ellook, Feris, Flamii, Gogol, Grebel, Griffox, Hox, Jagron, Kapiba, Mammut, Ories, Pippito, Ponio, Rapchor, Rhinon, Riik, Rodonya, Ropl, Runner, Sauros, Skwaror and Volff. Baigun Laias (Japanese: , Baigen Raia) are enemies in . They are members of the Laia family, and can be found at level 42-46 when salvaging at Battlescar Cove and Dalnes Stone in Temperantia and when salvaging at Port Anangham in the Empire of Mor Ardain during Bana's Secret Treasure.

The Avarr Driver (Japanese: , Avaru Doraibā) is a quest exclusive boss in . He is a Driver enemy who is fought at level 46 at the Fonsa Myma Port in the Kingdom of Uraya during Theory and Praxis, alongside the Firan and Torst Drivers.
The Basics of Tiger! Tiger! 1 are an Info Item in . They can be found in Tora's House, and provide an introduction to Tiger! Tiger!.
The Basics of Tiger! Tiger! 2 are an Info Item in . They can be found in Tora's House, and provide an introduction to Tiger! Tiger!.
The Basics of Tiger! Tiger! 3 are an Info Item in . They can be found in Tora's House, and provide an introduction to Tiger! Tiger!.

The Azure Driver (Japanese: , Azūra Doraibā) is a quest-exclusive enemy in . He is a Driver, and can be found at level 61 at the Cargo Transportation Zone in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the quest Farewell, Good Friend.

Baltro is an NPC in . He is an Urayan shopkeeper who can be found in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya, where he runs a shop called Proplater Blacksmiths which specializes in Core Chips. Baltro offers no quests or merc missions.

The Bana Etching Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Turf War Protection. It enables the purchase of Woodcut Prints of Bana from the Cmalaf Artwork shop in Torigoth in the Gormott Province.

The Bagna Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Frozen Door. It enables the purchase of Bagna Oyster Roll from the Tatraty Fish shop in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.

Baked Redfish are Key Items in . They can be purchased from the DLC Shops Famed Gourmet Chefs run by the Head Fire Dragon and a Fire Dragons Member at the Bellyfull Canteen in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the DLC Quest Midnight Feasting upon installing the New Quests Pack 1 of the Expansion Pass.

Azure Dragon Storm (Japanese: , Sōryūgeki) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using a Calamity Scythe. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Mòrag's Rising Dragon.
